headline: Nvidia's new liquid cooling system runs at 113°F (45°C) to cut water and electricity use
summary: Nvidia's new liquid cooling system for data centers runs at 113°F (45°C) to reduce electricity and water consumption. It claims up to 100% reduction in water use.
details: Nvidia has announced a new liquid cooling system for data centers that runs at a high temperature of 113°F (45°C). This system is designed to reduce electricity and water consumption, with claims of up to 100% reduction in water use.

The system uses a coolant composed of 75% water and 25% propylene glycol, which can exit the system at 131°F (55°C). This approach allows data centers to rely on outdoor dry coolers to expel heat to the environment, reducing the need for chillers.

Traditional water-cooling methods can account for nearly 40% of a data center's power consumption, while air-cooled facilities also use a considerable amount of electricity and generate noise pollution. Nvidia's new solution addresses some of the sustainability challenges faced by data centers.

The effectiveness of this system is most pronounced in regions with cooler climates, but it can still be effective in warmer areas as long as the ambient temperature is below 113°F (45°C). Data centers that experience occasional temperature swings above this limit may still need to use chillers, but less frequently.
